text:
incident-bot: ALERT 02:12 UTC — /api/v1/generate 502 rate > 12% for 5m, paging oncall

alex (oncall): Acked. Pushing to bridge now.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.company/bridges/2390012345 (auto)

alex (oncall): Quick context: sudden 502 spike, no deploy in last 30m. Traffic normal. Rolling errors start at ~02:08.

sara: Looking at logs, upstream pool returning 502s from model-runtime: "kv-cache timeout" visible. Investigating fallbacks.

jamie (ops lead): If runtime is flapping, let's switch the route to fallback-model-1 and scale the pool. Alex, can you trigger reroute?

alex (oncall): Doing reroute -> fallback-model-1 now.

incident-bot: ROUTE CHANGE: traffic routed to fallback-model-1, 30% capacity.

tom (eng-sre): I see a burst of long tail p95 on kv-store, likely GC/oom churn on a subset of nodes. Kicking a quick restart of the three affected pods.

alex (oncall): Restart issued for runtime-3a/3b/3c. Monitoring.

sara: After restart, 502s dropped to ~0.6% in 90s. Good.

maria (pm): Customer impact — internal tracking shows ~120 requests failed from two customers between 02:08-02:14. No large scale outage. Notifying account teams.

jamie (ops lead): Nice containment. Two followups we need before we close: postmortem, and alert rule tuning to prevent noisy paging for transient kv hiccups.

alex (oncall): I'm still on the bridge for another 15m then will hand off to @sara for post-incident.

sara: I'll take it. Plan: create postmortem doc + run a quick RCA. Can someone create the postmortem doc and assign owners?

jamie (ops lead): I'll create the postmortem doc. Link: https://docs.internal/postmortems/2390012345-kv-timeout-burst. Assigning owners: RCA -> @tom, remediation -> @jamie, customer-notify -> @maria.

tom (eng-sre): Taking RCA. Early hypothesis: KV cache pressure + GC pause + single-node hot shard. Will collect traces and runtime metrics.

maria (pm): I'll draft the customer notes and notify affected accounts during EOD.

jamie (ops lead): Action items (quick list):
- A1: Instrument per-shard kv metrics + alert if >70% tail latency 2m -> owner tom -> ticket #INC-5821
- A2: Adjust pager policy: require 3m sustained 5% 502 at cluster-level before paging (avoid single-shard noise) -> owner jamie -> ticket #OPS-7702
- A3: Add automatic short-circuit to fallback-model for kv timeout > 200ms -> owner alex -> ticket #RTE-3344
- A4: Postmortem writeup + timeline + mitigation steps -> owner sara -> ticket #PM-9910

alex (oncall): I'll create RTE-3344 now and add the small config patch.

incident-bot: Ticket created: RTE-3344.

tom (eng-sre): For A1, I'll add shard-level histograms and a dashboard. Also will open a small change to increase the kv-client circuit breaker from 50ms -> 150ms as a temporary hedge. Patch proposal in #git:runtime/patches/kv-cb-239001.

jamie (ops lead): Re: A2 (pager policy) — suggestion: change alert expression to something like:
```
alert: High502Cluster
expr: sum(rate(http_responses_total{code="502"}[3m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[3m])) > 0.05
for: 3m
```
That keeps bursty single-node noise from paging. Thoughts?\

tom (eng-sre): Looks good. Also add a label severity=warning if <0.2% and only escalate to page for severity=critical.

sara: Scheduled postmortem writing session tomorrow 10:30PT. Please block 30m.

maria (pm): Noted. Will prepare customer impact section beforehand.

alex (oncall): Handing off bridge to @sara. I'm done for oncall window.

sara: Acknowledged. Thanks @alex.

jamie (ops lead): I'll follow up on the alert rule change and test it in staging today. Will link PR in the postmortem doc.

tom (eng-sre): Action updates: started data collection, will have preliminary traces in 2-3 hours.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring.

maria (pm): Customer comms queued. No major escalation expected.

sara: Closing out live bridge. Going to convert this thread into the postmortem doc comments. If anyone has additional logs/traces, drop in the doc or ping me. :heart:

jamie (ops lead): TL;DR: fast containment via fallback routing + pod restart. Followups are alert tuning, per-shard metrics, and a small runtime config patch. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
